descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · S10 Existing specs: every AI call logs the vendor's time apart from the total and names the model that answered

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U8 Each run logs how long the AI call itself took, separately from the total, so a slow run can be traced to the AI service or to the app (UAT 3.5)
  • U7 The output records which model produced it; each run records which AI ran each step (note model, speech-to-text engine, pre-round model, photo model, Ask AI model) (UAT OAT-03 Expected Result 3; UAT 3.1; UAT 3.9; TFA-94422 AC 6; TFA-94423 AC 7)

Test design technique: Performance (performance) — Measure the time and check it is within the required seconds.

Given Local backend, diagnostics cleared; a stubbed Haiku → Mistral fallback through a real aiAction

When Call each AI action kind; run the stubbed fallback; run the normal path; run a call that fails before any answer

Then Each aiCallLog row has providerMs (a number) and durationMs ≥ providerMs, and the ai_disclosure audit row carries provider_ms / duration_ms; after a fallback the log has model = Mistral and fellBackFrom = Haiku and the audit row model / fell_back_from; the normal path has no fellBackFrom; …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Playwright api assertions. The speech-to-text engine is stored per call: aiAction writes an aiCallLog row and an ai_disclosure audit row for transcribe.prepareSession (model = the live route's model, e.g. gpt-live-transcribe) and transcribe.transcribeAudio (model = the batch model, e.g. …

Where it ran: local lane A (existing Playwright tests); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S10 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-03.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16/17 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane A.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: PERF · Performance timing — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: matrix (lane A).

UAT item: OAT-03 Retry/Timeout Resiliency · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-03/S10

Existing specs: every AI call logs the vendor's time apart from the total and names the model that answered

Tickets: TFA-94422 Haiku primary, Mistral fallback via Bedrock (ready for qa); TFA-94423 Implement GPT-live medical mode for active dictation (ready for qa)

Result: passed in matrix/OAT-03.results.json (lane A: the existing Playwright specs below, run on the local stack; agent-matrix.sh).

Existing specs:

  • api/ai-call-timing.spec.ts [api] — an AI call's log row and audit row carry the total and the vendor's time — expected
  • api/ai-call-timing.spec.ts [api] — every kind of AI call item 7 names logs the vendor's time — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-01 log shows the answering model — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-01 log shows the answering model (twin): no fallback, Haiku and no fellBackFrom — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-02 audit row shows it too — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04 a failure before any answer keeps the pre-resolved model — expected

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (Tim's api specs ai-call-timing.spec.ts and provider-fallback.spec.ts): a stubbed Haiku → Mistral fallback through a real aiAction on the local backend, with aiCallLog and audit rows read through the admin key.. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
